issues.legal_issue: A government sanction deleting an exemption rule must be read consistently with the corporation’s recommendation that exemptions already granted continue when the sanction does not show an intention to depart from that recommendation.
material_facts: The corporation recommended deleting the exemption rule while expressly preserving exemptions already granted until their respective periods expired.

The government’s sanction referred to the municipal commissioner’s letter and sanctioned deletion, but did not expressly reject the preservation condition or refer the proposal back for reconsideration.
The industrialists had relied on the corporation’s representations and obtained exemptions under the rule.
issues.conclusion: The government sanction incorporated, by necessary intendment, the condition that exemptions already granted would continue until their respective periods expired.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 149(2) of the Bombay Provincial Municipal Corporations Act, 1949, the government may refuse a proposed rule, refer it back, or sanction it with or without permissible modifications. The context and the materials referred to in the sanction showed that it followed the corporation’s recommendation without modification. Consistently with section 7 of the Bombay General Clauses Act, an amendment affecting individual legal rights is presumed prospective unless retrospective effect is expressed or implied.

predicates.challenge_to_withdrawal_of_existing_exem: A proceeding challenged a government action said to withdraw an exemption already granted to beneficiaries.
predicates.corporation_recommended_preserving_grant: The corporation recommended deleting the exemption rule while preserving exemptions already granted for their respective periods.
predicates.government_sanction_did_not_show_departu: The government sanctioned deletion without clearly rejecting the preservation condition or sending the proposal back for reconsideration.
predicates.beneficiaries_relied_on_existing_grants: The beneficiaries acted in reliance on representations and exemptions granted under the existing rule.
predicates.existing_exemptions_continue_for_their_g: Exemptions already granted remain effective until the periods for which they were granted expire.

issues.definition: When a challenge concerns withdrawal of an existing exemption, and the corporation recommended preserving existing grants, the government’s sanction did not show a contrary intention, and beneficiaries relied on those grants, the grants continue for their granted periods.

issues.legal_issue: The government cannot modify a corporation’s proposed tax rule so as to expand the levy’s application beyond the limits permitted for modifications.
material_facts: The corporation recommended deleting the exemption rule while retaining exemptions already granted.
If the government’s sanction were read as unconditionally withdrawing those exemptions, the tax rules would apply to areas where they had not previously applied.
Section 149(2) limited the government’s power to modify the corporation’s recommendation where the modification would increase the rate or extent of the levy.
issues.conclusion: The sanction had to be read as preserving exemptions already granted; an unconditional withdrawal that expanded the application of the levy would be legally infirm.
issues.legal_principle: Section 149(2) of the Bombay Provincial Municipal Corporations Act, 1949 permits modifications to the corporation’s proposed rules only within the statutory restriction against increasing the rate or extent of the levy. The Court treated an unconditional withdrawal of the exemptions as extending the rules to an area where they had not applied, and read the sanction down to avoid that result.

predicates.challenge_to_withdrawal_of_existing_exem: A proceeding challenged a government action said to withdraw an exemption already granted to beneficiaries.
predicates.unconditional_withdrawal_would_expand_le: Removing existing exemptions would cause the tax rules to apply to persons or areas to which they had not previously applied.
predicates.government_sanction_cannot_unconditional: The government action cannot be treated as unconditionally withdrawing existing exemptions where doing so would impermissibly expand the levy’s application.

issues.definition: When a challenge concerns withdrawal of an existing exemption and unconditional withdrawal would expand the levy’s application, the government action cannot unconditionally withdraw that exemption.

issues.legal_issue: A petition dismissed in limine should be remitted for consideration where additional issues remain to be decided and the petitioner may be able to establish entitlement under the governing order.
material_facts: The appeal arose from a High Court order dismissing a petition in limine.
The appellant had been allotted a demarcated plot but had not executed a sale deed.
Additional legal points remained, and whether the appellant qualified for the benefit depended on proof that it fell within the governing order.
issues.conclusion: The appeal was allowed and the matter remitted to the High Court to readmit and decide the petition according to law, with the appellant required to establish that it qualified under the governing order.
issues.legal_principle: The Court had already determined the interpretation of the government order in the connected appeals, but held that the petition should not have been dismissed in limine because additional legal points remained and the appellant’s qualification depended on proof. No earlier case was cited for this procedural ruling.

predicates.appeal_from_petition_dismissed_in_limine: A party appealed from an order dismissing its petition without a full hearing.
predicates.additional_issues_remain: Legal or factual issues material to the petition remain undecided.
predicates.entitlement_depends_on_facts_not_yet_pro: The petitioner’s entitlement depends on facts that have not yet been established.
predicates.petition_should_be_remitted_for_hearing_: The petition should be restored and sent for consideration and decision after the remaining issues are addressed.

issues.definition: When an appeal is from a petition dismissed in limine, material issues remain undecided, and entitlement depends on unproved facts, the petition should be remitted for a hearing and decision.
